chronologies.date: “I shall speak of the king who reigned next, whose name was Sesostris”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.102 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 136 (PDF p. 138)
chronologies.note: Sesostris follows Moeris and campaigns through Asia to Scythia and Thrace (2.102–110). Order agrees with CFAH: Moeris dies about 1679 BC (AP-17) and Sesostris (Senusret III) establishes the astronomical college in 1576 BC (AP-18); CFAH-3 Table 2 lists "Shortly after Moeris" as a match. Generations dates Senusret III about 1800 BC (the provisional sort) and 1614–1575 BC (Preparing, 2nd ed.).
